$comment: Single source of truth for imagery. `npm run manifest` regenerates prompts/image-manifest.md from this file. Drop a real file into public/images/<kind>/<filename> and the placeholder plate is replaced automatically at build time.

images.subject: A large organic form built from fine contour lines — like a topographic map of something that is not a landscape — with loose watercolour blooms of teal, slate blue, amber, coral and magenta washing through it, and a scatter of small ink dots joined by hairlines, as if a network had been traced over the top. It should read at once as weather, as a cell, as a root system and as a map, without settling into any of them.
images.concept: The hidden systems the book keeps pointing at, drawn once, on the outside.
images.purpose: The front cover. Carries the whole book's promise before a word is read.
images.revision: Warm cream ground (#F3EFE5) that can be knocked out to transparent. Keep the top third quiet — the title sits there. No legible text anywhere in the artwork.

images.spread: Back cover, beneath the handwritten line
images.subject: A small botanical ink drawing in the manner of a nineteenth-century field guide: a cluster of mushrooms with their mycelium threads visible below the soil line, drawn in fine charcoal hatching on warm cream, no colour.
images.concept: The visible part, and the part doing the work.
images.purpose: Back cover. Quiet counterweight to the front.
images.revision: Fine hatching only. The mycelium below the line is the point — do not crop it out.

images.essay: Why Ordinary Days May Be the Point of Life
images.subject: A photograph of a dog asleep in a rectangle of afternoon light on a bare floor, overprinted with the full solar geometry that produced it: sun altitude and azimuth for the hour, the window aperture in plan, the projected parallelogram of light plotted on the floorboards with its dimensions in millimetres, and the dog's position marked as the optimum. Survey linework in moss over a warm photograph, the light patch itself glowing amber.
images.concept: The quietest possible image, surveyed.
images.purpose: Essay opener. Establishes on page one that this book measures things, and that the first thing it measures is a dog asleep.
images.revision: Specimen colour moss #68735B on the key lines and the label chip. The overlay must be drafted, not sketched — real angles, real units. It should take a beat before the reader realises the diagram is serious.

images.essay: Why Ordinary Days May Be the Point of Life
images.subject: A specimen card for a coffee mug left where it was put down: catalogue number, date, time, a small measured elevation drawing of the mug, and dry entries — 'displacement since Tuesday: 4 cm', 'contents: cold', 'placed without decision'. Ruled card stock, ink, one moss chip.
images.concept: The mundane object, accessioned.
images.purpose: Taped inset. Interrupts the first text spread at a conceptual turn, not for decoration.
images.revision: Specimen colour moss #68735B. Handwriting only in the annotations; the form itself is printed. No legible paragraph text.

images.essay: Why Ordinary Days May Be the Point of Life
images.subject: A bathymetric map of an ordinary lake — depth contours in lake blue with soundings, algae-green shallows, a dashed line tracing the path walked around it, and one small cross where the walker always stops without knowing why. Printed like a mid-century survey sheet, with a legend and a north arrow.
images.concept: A place you have already stopped seeing, drawn by someone who did not.
images.purpose: Reading spread plate. Pairs with the observational drawing opposite.
images.revision: Specimen colour moss #68735B on the walked path and the chip; the water carries lake and algae. The cross gets no explanation anywhere on the plate.

images.essay: Why Ordinary Days May Be the Point of Life
images.subject: The ordinary photograph nobody would keep — a broad, flat view of a path beside water — corner-mounted on cream card with a pencil note beneath it and a torn strip of the previous week's tide table taped alongside. Deliberately unremarkable, deliberately well presented.
images.concept: What the place is showing you.
images.purpose: Left half of the pair. Must be genuinely dull, and framed as though it were not.
images.revision: Specimen colour moss #68735B. The mounting is immaculate; the photograph is not. That contrast is the whole left-hand page.

images.essay: Why Ordinary Days May Be the Point of Life
images.subject: One drop of water from the view opposite, at 400×: diatoms, rotifers, desmids and a ciliate mid-turn, in saturated bioluminescent teal, acid green, coral and cobalt against a dark ground. A real scale bar reading 50 µm, and a small key numbering four organisms.
images.concept: What the place was doing the whole time.
images.purpose: Right half of the pair, and the loudest plate in Part I. The payoff for a page of politeness.
images.revision: Specimen colour moss #68735B on the chip only — the plate itself is full spectrum and must be the most saturated thing in the first forty pages. This is the image that proves Stage I is quiet in layout, not in colour.

images.essay: Why Ordinary Days May Be the Point of Life
images.subject: A patent-style mechanical schematic of one step taken across a kitchen: centre-of-mass arc, ground reaction vectors, the firing order of eleven muscles numbered in sequence, ankle and hip moments, and an inset control-loop block diagram labelled 'balance, closed loop, unattended'. Fig. numbers throughout. Drafted in hairline ink on bone.
images.concept: An astonishing biological achievement, performed absent-mindedly.
images.purpose: Carries the walking passage. The essay calls it astonishing in one sentence; this spends a whole page proving it.
images.revision: Specimen colour moss #68735B on the key lines, amber on the force vectors. Deadpan — no cartoon figure, no exaggeration. It should look like it was filed with a patent office.

images.essay: Why Ordinary Days May Be the Point of Life
images.subject: A pinned specimen card of something that cannot be pinned: a shadow across pavement — a railing, a branch, a person out of frame, printed small and mounted on ruled card with an entomologist's label carrying only the time and the condition — '3:42 PM / wind from west'. Two brass pins, a ruled border, one moss chip.
images.concept: Noticed, not explained.
images.purpose: One of three on the contact sheet. The labels record what was noticed and nothing else.
images.revision: Specimen colour moss #68735B. The label must be shorter than feels comfortable. No caption anywhere explains why the thing was worth mounting.

Two brass pins, a ruled border, one moss chip.

images.essay: Why Ordinary Days May Be the Point of Life
images.subject: The same stretch of lakeshore in spring, identical framing, overprinted with that visit's measurements set in a small ruled block: leaf area 0.4 · day length 12h 41m · water 7 °C · 3 species calling. The photograph is unremarkable; the data is exact.
images.concept: The route repeats. The world does not.
images.purpose: Frame of four in the sequence strip. The frame must not move between visits — the data is the only thing allowed to change.
images.revision: Specimen colour moss #68735B on the chip; the overlay block shifts to moss for this frame, so the strip reads as a colour ramp across the seasons before a single figure is read.

images.essay: Why Ordinary Days May Be the Point of Life
images.subject: An album leaf: one photograph of someone standing in kitchen light, corner-mounted, surrounded by the residue of an ordinary life — a grocery receipt, a note in handwriting, a pressed leaf, a ticket stub — arranged with care on aged cream. Nothing legible enough to read as text.
images.concept: The extraordinary person, become the person in the kitchen.
images.purpose: Crossover band. The one place in the essay where the apparatus stops and the book just looks at somebody.
images.revision: Specimen colour moss #68735B. Keep the figure fully on one page; nothing of interest within 15 mm of the fold. No measurement, no key, no diagram anywhere on this spread — it earns its silence by following six pages of instruments.

images.essay: Why Ordinary Days May Be the Point of Life
images.subject: The last leaf of a field notebook: one photograph taped in — late-afternoon lake, an empty path, or a dog walking away — with a single line of handwriting beneath it and three-quarters of the page left blank. The ruling shows through.
images.concept: The book putting you back down where it found you.
images.purpose: Closing image. Not spectacular; that is the requirement, not a limitation.
images.revision: Specimen colour moss #68735B, used once, small. The blank is doing the work — do not fill it.

images.subject: A lit second-floor window at dusk, its glass carrying the reflection of the street trees behind the viewer, overprinted with two complete figure-ground diagrams keyed to the same surface: one tracing the room, one tracing the reflection, in two colours at the same weight. Both are correct. The eye cannot hold them at once.
images.concept: Two worlds occupying one surface.
images.purpose: Essay opener. States the premise as an optical fact before the essay states it as a sentence.
images.revision: Specimen colour lake #3E6B87 for the room trace, coral for the reflection trace, equal weight — if one recedes the plate has failed. No caption tells the reader to try.

images.spread: Unplaced. Freed when the reproduced record took the pull-quote verso.
images.subject: A field-guide plate of a single room drawn twice on one card: once complete in fine hairline ink, once as the four or five marks that survived being looked at. The second drawing sits beside the first at the same scale, mostly empty.
images.concept: The paraphrase. What the editor kept.
images.purpose: Gives the pull quote something to argue with rather than decorate.
images.revision: Specimen colour lake #3E6B87 on the complete drawing; the surviving marks print in signal-bright so the eye finds them first. Same scale, same position — the comparison is the plate. Made and in the repo, currently not on any page. The pull-quote spread it held now carries the 31 inferred ad categories instead.

images.subject: A time-motion plate of an old dog and a rectangle of afternoon light: the light patch plotted at six successive times in tinted outline, the dog's position at each, displacement arrows in centimetres per hour, and the dent left in a rug marked as the datum. Ethological in tone, with a legend and a scale.
images.concept: Sustained attention without effort. The animal is better at this than you are.
images.purpose: Carries the essay's central practical claim: noticing is a matter of speed, not will.
images.revision: Specimen colour lake #3E6B87 on the key lines, amber for the six light patches so the sequence reads as time. Absolutely straight-faced — this is a real figure about a dog being better at the subject than the author.

images.subject: An enormous flat bank of weather over a grey lake, one very small figure standing on a breakwater far right of centre, overprinted with the faintest possible synoptic layer: two isobars and a frontal boundary crossing the sky, drawn so lightly they could be missed on the first pass.
images.concept: Scale as an attention device. The eye has to travel to find the person, and then travel again to find the weather map.
images.purpose: The book's first long exhale. No text, no folio.
images.revision: Specimen colour lake #3E6B87, at the lowest weight anywhere in the book. If the overlay is noticed before the figure, it is too strong. Keep the horizon clear of the fold; the figure sits fully on the recto.

images.subject: Starlings scattered on a wire above a wet sidewalk, arranged by accident into something that reads like handwriting — presented as a comparison: the photograph, the birds traced off it as pure marks, and a line of real handwriting set beneath at matching scale, with a small key. Assembled on cream, taped.
images.concept: The world composing itself without intending to.
images.purpose: Opens Part I on a pattern that was always there, and on the book's method: notice, trace, compare, say nothing.
images.revision: Specimen colour lake #3E6B87. The three elements must be the same width and stacked, so the resemblance does the arguing. No caption points it out.

images.subject: Four branching systems at one scale and one line weight: a river delta, a root mass, a street grid, a capillary bed.
images.concept: The same structural logic arriving in four unrelated materials.
images.purpose: The divider for Part II. It has to say "look at the pattern, not the thing" before a single essay does.
images.revision: A screen print of a forest horizon was tried here and pulled. See content/plan/screen-print.md.

images.essay: The Beauty of Systems Nobody Designed
images.subject: A line of ants crossing pavement, rerouting around a crack, close and low.
images.concept: A path maintained without a map.
images.purpose: The essay opens on this. Evidence that a route can be held by contact alone.

images.essay: The Beauty of Systems Nobody Designed
images.subject: A starling flock changing direction above bare winter trees, one coherent moving edge.
images.concept: Local corrections producing a single shape.
images.purpose: Band under a two-column reading spread. The margin note beside it is the topological-distance finding.

images.essay: The Beauty of Systems Nobody Designed
images.subject: A slime mold network on a dish: thick trunks along useful routes, thin branches withdrawing.
images.concept: A useful map made by something with no brain and no nervous system.
images.purpose: Band under the spread that carries the Tokyo experiment. The picture has to make the network legible as a network, not as mold.

images.essay: The Beauty of Systems Nobody Designed
images.subject: A sectional drawing of a subterranean termite nest: parallel floors, connected ramps, chambers.
images.concept: Colony-scale architecture from local building acts.
images.purpose: Drawn rather than photographed, because the whole point is a section nobody can stand back and see.

images.essay: The Beauty of Systems Nobody Designed
images.subject: A worn track cutting a corner across grass, beside the paved path it ignores.
images.concept: The most literal case in the essay, and the one the photo library does not contain.
images.purpose: Faces the pull quote. See content/plan/photo-selection-04.md — this is on the shoot list.

images.subject: A plan-view survey of one street corner: four figures at a crosswalk drawn from above, each sight-line plotted to a different object and labelled — a phone, a pigeon, a shop sign, nothing in particular — with their overlapping shadows outlined as a single shape and given its own hatch. Legend, scale bar, north arrow.
images.concept: Four separate paraphrases of one street corner.
images.purpose: Interrupts the text at the foot of the verso, so the spread has weight where it would otherwise trail off.
images.revision: Specimen colour lake #3E6B87 on the sight-lines. The corner is surveyed with the seriousness of a battlefield plan. The label reading 'nothing in particular' is the only joke and it is not flagged.

images.subject: A set of six to eight short handwritten annotations in brown-black iron-gall ink on transparent ground, cut from a nineteenth-century manuscript or field notebook. Two or three words each, plus an underline, a bracket, a caret and a small pointing arrow. Visible pressure variation, a blot, one crossing-out.
images.concept: A hand in the margin of a machine-set page.
images.purpose: The set is otherwise entirely machine-set — monospace, engraved labels, printed tables. A real hand introduces the person doing the noticing.
images.revision: Transparent PNG, ink only, no paper ground — it sits on the book's own paper. Must NOT be legible as sentences; it reads as a gesture.

images.spread: Overlay across a diagram or plate
images.subject: A single longer handwritten passage, four or five lines, running at a slight angle across the frame, as though written over a printed figure after the fact. Same iron-gall ink, transparent ground.
images.concept: Someone argued with the diagram.
images.purpose: Breaks the authority of a printed figure — the book is observation, not instruction.
images.revision: Transparent PNG. Angle no more than 3°. Illegible as text at reading distance.

images.credit: Composited from Poly Haven's “Rough Linen” diffuse, displacement and ambient-occlusion maps, relit from the side for this book
images.subject: Raw undyed linen at macro scale, lit raking from one side so the weave throws its own shadows. Individual slubs and thread irregularities clearly visible. No hem, no edge, no object — only surface.
images.concept: The cover, from the inside.
images.purpose: The set is entirely pigment on cellulose. One genuinely different material makes the paper read as chosen rather than defaulted — and linen rhymes with the binding.
images.revision: Warm neutral, close to the book's paper in value so the break is tactile rather than tonal.

images.credit: Composited from Poly Haven's “Rusty Metal 04” PBR maps and a photograph of weathered copper by Lana on Unsplash, relit and rebalanced for this book
images.subject: Oxidised copper or weathered steel at macro scale — rust bloom, verdigris, mineral crust. Raking light. Reads as a landscape until you realise the scale is wrong.
images.concept: Time, doing its work on something that was supposed to last.
images.purpose: The hardest material break in the book, placed where the book is most vivid.
images.revision: Let the rust carry the accent colours of Stage IV — coral, ultraviolet — rather than importing them.

images.credit: Composited from glass-droplet photography by Petri R on Unsplash, over a heavily blurred atmosphere layer from a condensation photograph by Lana on Unsplash; no scene from either remains legible
images.subject: Condensation on a cold window at macro scale, with the world beyond it entirely out of focus. Droplets holding tiny inverted images of whatever is outside.
images.concept: A surface you look through, photographed as a surface.
images.purpose: The turn back to calm. Transparent material after opaque ones.
images.revision: The out-of-focus world must be unreadable — the moment it resolves into a scene it stops being a material.

images.essay: Why Ordinary Days May Be the Point of Life
images.subject: A plotted study of habituation: forty or fifty fine response curves, each starting high at the left and decaying toward a flat line as the same stimulus repeats, overlaid so they form a soft descending band. Small plotted points along each curve. Two or three tiny circular inset diagrams at the margins, drawn like detail figures. A single very diffuse wash of faded moss green sitting low. **Composition: the curves have already flattened across the upper two-thirds, so that area is nearly empty — two columns of body copy sit there. The density is in the lower third, at the left where the curves begin.**
images.concept: The measured shape of a thing becoming ordinary.
images.purpose: This essay's argument is that repetition dulls response. The ground is that claim, plotted — the reader is reading about habituation on top of a picture of it.
images.revision: Transparent PNG. Ink linework and plotted points, plus at most ONE very diffuse wash of a single colour — no hard edges on the wash. It is laid under body copy at 8% (14% on a dark page), so linework stays hairline and the wash stays soft enough to survive being nearly invisible. No text, numerals, labels or legends anywhere.

images.spread: Under the essay opener or a reading spread
images.subject: A signal-filtering plate: a dense field of hundreds of small plotted points and short vectors at one edge, funnelling through a narrow constriction drawn as a few converging hairlines, and emerging on the other side as a mere handful of points. Fine annotation arcs around the constriction, and one tiny human figure at the output side for scale. A diffuse wash of faded cobalt around the dense side only. **Composition: the dense input field occupies the outer third; the middle and inner thirds are sparse, because that is where the title and text sit.**
images.concept: Everything the room was doing, and the fraction that got through.
images.purpose: The essay says attention is an editor writing a very short summary. This draws the edit.
images.revision: Transparent PNG. Ink linework and plotted points, plus at most ONE very diffuse wash of a single colour — no hard edges on the wash. It is laid under body copy at 8% (14% on a dark page), so linework stays hairline and the wash stays soft enough to survive being nearly invisible. No text, numerals, labels or legends anywhere.

images.essay: The Beauty of Systems Nobody Designed
images.spread: Under a reading or image-pair spread
images.subject: A flocking study: several hundred tiny directional marks, each a short line with a head, arranged so that local alignment builds into one large coherent sweep across the frame without any centre or leader. Fine dotted radius circles around a few individual marks, showing the neighbourhood each one responds to. A diffuse wash of lake blue following the sweep. **Composition: the sweep enters low at one side and exits low at the other, leaving the upper half open for text.**
images.concept: Three local rules, and a shape nobody specified.
images.purpose: The essay's claim is that the pattern exists between the parts. This shows the between.
images.revision: Transparent PNG. Ink linework and plotted points, plus at most ONE very diffuse wash of a single colour — no hard edges on the wash. It is laid under body copy at 8% (14% on a dark page), so linework stays hairline and the wash stays soft enough to survive being nearly invisible. No text, numerals, labels or legends anywhere. Runs across the fold: keep the densest area off the centre 30 mm.

images.subject: A distributed-system plate: one small node, drawn as a tiny human figure, with fine lines radiating out to a dozen external nodes of varying size — each node a small circular diagram in its own right, some plotted with points, some with concentric rings. The lines are weighted by nothing; all are hairlines. Diffuse amber wash pooling at the outer nodes, not at the figure. **Composition: the figure sits low and off-centre; the network fans upward and outward into the corners, leaving a clear diagonal band through the middle for text.**
images.concept: The thinking that is not happening inside the head.
images.purpose: The essay argues intelligence is not what a brain does alone. The centre is deliberately the smallest node.
images.revision: Transparent PNG. Ink linework and plotted points, plus at most ONE very diffuse wash of a single colour — no hard edges on the wash. It is laid under body copy at 8% (14% on a dark page), so linework stays hairline and the wash stays soft enough to survive being nearly invisible. No text, numerals, labels or legends anywhere.

images.essay: The Strange Privilege of Being Alive During a Technological Revolution
images.subject: A compression study on a dark field: two long hairlines running the width of the frame, one labelled by position as intent and the other as artefact, with fine vertical connectors between them. At the left the connectors are long; they shorten steadily until at the right the two lines nearly touch. Small plotted points where each connector meets a line. A diffuse bioluminescent teal wash where the lines converge. **Composition: convergence at the outer edge, the open end at the inner — the wide, sparse left two-thirds carries the reversed-out text.**
images.concept: The gap between imagining a thing and making it, closing.
images.purpose: The essay is about that gap. Drawn, it needs no caption.
images.revision: Transparent PNG with PALE lines on a dark page — white or near-white ink, not charcoal. Ink linework and plotted points, plus at most ONE very diffuse wash of a single colour — no hard edges on the wash. It is laid under body copy at 8% (14% on a dark page), so linework stays hairline and the wash stays soft enough to survive being nearly invisible. No text, numerals, labels or legends anywhere.

images.essay: The Last Generation That Remembers the Before-Time
images.subject: A density plot on a dark field: a scatter of several hundred tiny outlined objects — rectangles, discs, spools, spirals, drawn small enough to read as marks rather than as things — crowded densely at one edge and thinning steadily across the frame until only three or four remain. One tiny human figure standing at the point where the density breaks. Diffuse ultraviolet wash at the dense edge. **Composition: dense at the outer edge, nearly empty across the inner two-thirds where the text sits.**
images.concept: A world of objects, becoming one object.
images.purpose: The essay is a count of what disappeared. This is the count.
images.revision: Transparent PNG with PALE lines on a dark page. Ink linework and plotted points, plus at most ONE very diffuse wash of a single colour — no hard edges on the wash. It is laid under body copy at 8% (14% on a dark page), so linework stays hairline and the wash stays soft enough to survive being nearly invisible. No text, numerals, labels or legends anywhere.

images.spread: Under a reading or pull-quote spread
images.subject: A route study: two dozen fine wandering lines entering from every edge of the frame and converging on a single point, each drawn as a real walked path would be — meandering, doubling back, not straight. Small plotted points at irregular intervals along each route, like recorded stops. A diffuse rust wash around the convergence. **Composition: the convergence point sits low and well off-centre; the upper half is open, sparse route lines only, because a large quote sits there.**
images.concept: Many separate walks, arriving at the same place.
images.purpose: Pilgrimage drawn as data rather than as devotion.
images.revision: Transparent PNG. Ink linework and plotted points, plus at most ONE very diffuse wash of a single colour — no hard edges on the wash. It is laid under body copy at 8% (14% on a dark page), so linework stays hairline and the wash stays soft enough to survive being nearly invisible. No text, numerals, labels or legends anywhere.

images.spread: Under the closing spread of the book
images.subject: Nested systems drawn as concentric irregular rings — six of them, each a different kind of line: cellular stipple at the innermost, then a branching vascular line, then a street-grid fragment, then an ecological web, then a circuit trace, then a slow astronomical arc at the outermost. One very small human figure standing near the centre, no larger than a few millimetres at full size. Diffuse warm amber wash at the centre only, fading outward to nothing. **Composition: the rings are concentric but the whole figure sits low and to one side, so the upper outer quadrant is nearly empty for the final words.**
images.concept: Body, family, city, ecosystem, technology, time — and one person inside all of them.
images.purpose: The last ground in the book, and the one that gathers every system the other seven drew separately. It should be the only ground a reader consciously notices.
images.revision: Transparent PNG. Ink linework and plotted points, plus at most ONE very diffuse wash of a single colour — no hard edges on the wash. It is laid under body copy at 8% (14% on a dark page), so linework stays hairline and the wash stays soft enough to survive being nearly invisible. No text, numerals, labels or legends anywhere. The six rings must each be a visibly different kind of line, or it collapses into a target.

images.subject: The same watercolour-and-ink systems drawing as the existing cover artwork, but composed inside a single circle: a bounded circular field of view, hard-edged, sitting on warm cream paper with nothing outside it. Inside the circle, read as a whole world without ever resolving into the Earth — broad atmospheric bands of teal and slate curving with the sphere near one limb; a swirl of current or weather blooming in rust, amber and coral across the middle; fine contour lines banding the surface the way isobars band a planet; a branching network of hairlines running through it like root systems or river deltas or blood vessels, deliberately impossible to say which. Small plotted points and connecting lines scattered across it. Two or three tiny human figures standing at the very edge of the circle, at the scale of a millimetre, so the size of the thing is unmistakable. A few small circular inset diagrams outside the main circle, in the cream, like detail figures from the same study.
images.concept: A circular field of view is the drawing an astronomer and a microscopist both make. At this scale it could be a planet or it could be a single drop of pond water, and the book cannot tell you which — which is the argument: the scale is arbitrary, the attention is what changes.
images.purpose: An alternative cover artwork for the `orb` treatment. A circle on a square is the strongest graphic move available on a 300 mm cover, and it makes the title's 'here' mean somewhere.
images.revision: Transparent PNG or warm cream ground. **Not the Earth**: no recognisable continents, no coastlines, no blue-marble colouring, no latitude/longitude graticule, no space, no stars, no glow or lens flare, no terminator line dividing day from night. The circle is drawn — very slightly out of true, with a hand-inked edge — not rendered as a lit sphere. Keep the upper third of the circle quieter: on the `orb` cover the title sits above and slightly over it.

images.subject: The lake, on an ordinary afternoon. Boats moored, nothing happening at length.
images.concept: A personal interlude between parts.
images.purpose: Field note verso. The only place in the book where a real photograph of this life appears at size.
images.revision: Square centre-left crop of the 5712 × 3213 original, offset 349 px. Not retouched, not upscaled. 272 dpi at 300 mm.

images.subject: A lawnmower from directly above on a garage floor, grass still on the deck.
images.concept: A personal interlude between parts.
images.purpose: Field note verso. The machine before you are told what it wants.
images.revision: Square crop of the 3213 × 5712 original, 1049 px down. Not retouched, not upscaled. 272 dpi at 300 mm.

images.spread: Field note (recto, taped inset at 70 mm)
images.subject: The serial plate on a lawnmower engine: model number, barcode, QR, and the words “Data Rates apply.”
images.concept: A personal interlude between parts.
images.purpose: Field note verso. The only place in the book where a real photograph of this life appears at size.
images.selection: B005 · IMG_5199, Oct 2 2025 is only 883 × 597 px. See content/plan/photo-selection-02.md
images.revision: Native resolution, uncropped, unretouched. At 70 mm wide this is 320 dpi, which is why it works here and not as a full bleed. See content/plan/photo-selection-04.md.

images.section: Field note · A street with nothing on it
images.subject: An empty suburban street, wires overhead, two small figures stopped on the sidewalk.
images.concept: A personal interlude between parts.
images.purpose: Field note verso. The only place in the book where a real photograph of this life appears at size.
images.revision: Centre square crop of the 5712 × 3213 original. Not retouched, not upscaled. 272 dpi at 300 mm. OPEN: at square the two figures are large enough to read as a posed portrait facing the lens, which the candid rule forbids. See decisions.md.

images.subject: A fire pit at dusk, a figure seated in profile watching it, trees behind.
images.concept: A personal interlude between parts.
images.purpose: Field note verso. The only place in the book where a real photograph of this life appears at size.
images.revision: Square crop of the 4032 × 2268 original, offset 705 px to hold the dog and the lounger. Shadows not lifted. 192 dpi at 300 mm, which is under the 300 dpi ideal and acceptable for a dark, soft-edged frame.

images.section: Part III · The World Is Changing
images.subject: A room-sized computer, a fingernail-sized chip and a blinking cursor, drawn at one line weight on a dark ground.
images.concept: Fifty years of the same machine getting quieter.
images.purpose: The divider where the book inverts. Pale ink on charcoal, and the first page that is not cream.

images.subject: A figure at the edge of a river, back turned, watching a dog swim. Separated into three plates.
images.concept: The way back, and somebody standing still in it.
images.purpose: The divider that returns the book to warm paper after two dark parts. A screen print rather than a photograph, because the archive it came from is 1,280 px and could never be one.
images.revision: Separated at --simplify 700. The plates are masks; the ink comes from Stage V.

images.subject: A carpenter’s pencil line on a board, a tape measure beside it, the saw cut a few millimetres past the mark.
images.concept: A surface holding a decision after the number is forgotten.
images.purpose: The essay opens on this. Thinking that is on the wood, not in the head.

images.subject: Index cards being rearranged across a table, shot from directly above, one hand entering the frame.
images.concept: Position performing part of the thinking.
images.purpose: Band under the working-memory margin note. The arrangement has to look mid-move, not finished.

images.subject: A penguin underwater, wings out, against a field of light. Separated into three plates.
images.concept: A body that senses through the medium it is moving in.
images.purpose: Faces the pull quote. On a dark stage the plates composite normally and lay largest first.
images.revision: Separated at --simplify 700. Replaces the orb-web drawing, which stays a good idea for a diagram spread.

images.subject: A driver’s view: wet road ahead, a blue route line on a screen at the edge of frame, the turn not yet named.
images.concept: Navigation held by the device and the road together.
images.purpose: Band beside the taxi-driver margin note. No faces, no hands on the wheel if it can be avoided.

images.subject: A workbench with tools laid out ready for use, nobody present, the work half done.
images.concept: A room that is holding the next step.
images.purpose: The tall plate. It has to read as waiting, not as tidy.

images.section: Part III · The World Is Changing
images.subject: A kitchen table with an open laptop while domestic life continues around it: dishes, a chair pushed out, afternoon light.
images.concept: History happening inside an ordinary afternoon.
images.purpose: On the shoot list in photo-selection-04. The library has nothing like it.

images.section: Part III · The World Is Changing
images.subject: A room-sized computer, a microprocessor at fingernail scale and a plain chat window, each drawn as a found artefact rather than a timeline.
images.concept: A revolution ending in an ordinary interface.
images.purpose: Band under the 4004 margin note. Not an infographic, and no arrows between the three.

images.section: Part III · The World Is Changing
images.subject: A laptop showing a generated paragraph that stops mid-sentence, a printed page beside it marked up by hand.
images.concept: New capability and old judgment on the same desk.
images.purpose: Faces the pull quote. The handwriting must be legible as correction without being readable as content.

images.section: Part III · The World Is Changing
images.subject: Two people comparing machine-generated options on a screen, neither looking at the camera, mid-disagreement.
images.concept: Adoption happening through comparison rather than spectacle.
images.purpose: Band beside the transformer margin note. Candid rule applies; this is the one that will be tempting to stage.

images.section: Part III · The World Is Changing
images.subject: A dog asleep under a desk, cables and feet above her, the screen out of frame.
images.concept: From the floor, an extraordinary afternoon is a Tuesday.
images.purpose: On the shoot list in photo-selection-04, and the one image in the storyboard that is purely Adam’s to take.

images.section: Part III · The World Is Changing
images.subject: A folded road atlas open across a passenger seat, one fold split white, a coffee ring on the index.
images.concept: A route that had to stay visible without knowing where you were.
images.purpose: The opener. It has to look used rather than collected.

images.section: Part III · The World Is Changing
images.subject: An answering machine beside a landline in an empty room, one red digit lit.
images.concept: Absence with a physical sound and a fixed place.
images.purpose: Band under the adoption margin note. No hand, no person; the room has to be empty.

images.section: Part III · The World Is Changing
images.subject: A contact sheet of six film frames, at least two of them failed: a thumb, a closed eye, a blur.
images.concept: An image that arrived after the moment could no longer be corrected.
images.purpose: Faces the pull quote. The failures are the picture. Do not select good frames.

images.section: Part III · The World Is Changing
images.subject: Three people waiting under a station clock, none of them holding anything, none of them able to find out why the bus is late.
images.concept: Waiting with nothing to do.
images.purpose: Band beside the SMS margin note. If anyone in frame is holding a phone the picture is about something else.

images.section: Part III · The World Is Changing
images.subject: A phone book, a cassette, a paper ticket and a page of handwritten numbers, laid out without arrangement.
images.concept: Things that each did one thing.
images.purpose: The tall plate. Every function here now lives in one object in a pocket, and the caption says so.

images.subject: A stone threshold worn into a shallow bowl at its centre, raking light across the dip.
images.concept: Repetition become visible in architecture.
images.purpose: The opener. Nothing else in frame; the wear is the whole subject.

images.subject: A painted yellow arrow on a kerb, pointing down an ordinary lane between parked cars.
images.concept: A sacred route running through somewhere unremarkable.
images.purpose: Band under the Shikoku margin note. The banality of the lane is the point.

images.subject: One continuous footpath crossing towns, fields and contour lines toward a small final mark, drawn at a single hairline weight.
images.concept: Destination and duration held in one line.
images.purpose: Faces the pull quote. No scale bar, no place names, no legend.

images.subject: Two walkers sitting against a plain roadside wall, boots off, tending their feet.
images.concept: A meaningful route as a bodily task.
images.purpose: Band beside the Camino margin note. Photo-selection-04 has real candidates for this row.

images.subject: A folded paper credential open across a table, each stop stamped in a different ink.
images.concept: The proof of a walk is a document nobody checks.
images.purpose: The tall plate. Real stamps, uneven pressure, one of them upside down.

images.subject: A dog crossing from shadow into a narrow band of late light on a floor.
images.concept: An ordinary room changing continuously.
images.purpose: The closing essay opens where the book opened, which is the point.

images.subject: A sectional drawing of an ordinary house with the paths of sunlight, airflow, water, power and data running through it.
images.concept: Domestic calm depending on moving systems.
images.purpose: Band under the sunlight margin note. The house must be plain and the systems hairline.

images.subject: Two people in separate rooms connected by an open doorway, neither looking at the camera, neither aware of the other being photographed.
images.concept: A shared life continuing without performance.
images.purpose: Faces the pull quote, and is the closest the book comes to a portrait.

images.subject: Rain on a window: one drop meeting another and changing direction, the view behind entirely out of focus.
images.concept: Two things touching and both of them going somewhere else.
images.purpose: Band beside the Earth-motion margin note. Nothing beyond the glass may resolve.

images.subject: The last of the evening light on a far interior wall, under a minute from gone.
images.concept: The room does this whether or not anyone is in it.
images.purpose: The last tall plate in the book. It should be the quietest.
images.revision: A screen print of an empty room was tried here and pulled: a 4:3 separation cropped to 2:3 loses the window, which was the whole subject.

images.spread: Image essay, specimen card at 66 mm
images.subject: The head of a Komodo dragon at rest on sand, one eye open, nostril and jawline in raking light.
images.concept: An animal that finds direction by sampling the world rather than by modelling it.
images.purpose: A real record on a page that argues thinking happens outside the skull. Photographed by Adam, 2014. A captive animal — do not caption it as wild.
images.target: 1280 × 960 px (native — 493 dpi at 66 mm, and nothing larger)
images.revision: Not retouched, not upscaled. It is used at the only size its resolution supports.

images.essay: The Beauty of Systems Nobody Designed
images.spread: Image essay, specimen card at 66 mm
images.subject: A queen butterfly, Danaus gilippus, closed on a grass stem: chestnut ground, white spots scattered across the forewing, fine veins.
images.concept: Two toxic species converging on one warning pattern that neither of them chose.
images.purpose: The essay argues that a pattern can exist between the parts. This is one, and it is a real photograph rather than a drawn diagram.
images.target: 1280 × 960 px (native — 493 dpi at 66 mm, and nothing larger)
images.revision: NOT A MONARCH. Identified as Danaus gilippus by the chestnut ground, the white spots scattered mid-forewing and the absence of heavy black veins. It was logged as a monarch on first pass and that was wrong. Captive animal.
